title: Indian Airlines Flight 491

agencies.name: Directorate General of Civil Aviation
agencies.report_title: Civil Aviation Aircraft Accident Summary for the Year 1993

summary: Indian Airlines Flight 491, a Boeing 737-200, took off from Aurangabad Airport with 118 persons on board. The aircraft lifted off near the end of the 6,000-foot runway with inadequate rotation. Shortly after takeoff, the left landing gear and left engine struck a truck carrying cotton bales on a road adjacent to the runway at approximately 410 feet from the runway end. The impact damaged the aircraft's left landing gear, left engine thrust reverser, and control surfaces. The aircraft continued in flight but subsequently struck high-tension power lines approximately 3 km northeast of the airport and crashed, killing 55 persons.
probable_cause: The captain's error in initiating late rotation and following wrong rotation technique resulted in inadequate climb performance. Additionally, the airport authorities failed to regulate mobile traffic on the Beed Road during flight operations, allowing a truck to remain in the hazard zone near the runway end.

factors.evidence: Captain's false perception of takeoff technique resulted in late rotation and failure to achieve adequate liftoff altitude before the runway end (p. 1).
Pilot did not initiate rotation at appropriate airspeed or position on runway, resulting in aircraft lifting off near end of 6,000-foot runway; error in rotation technique (p. 1).
Airport authorities failed to regulate or exclude mobile traffic from Beed Road adjacent to runway during flight operations (p. 1).
Aircraft's left main landing gear and left engine thrust reverser were severed; left elevator and horizontal stabilizer damaged by collision with truck (p. 1).
Aircraft impacted high-tension electric wires approximately 3 km northeast of runway and struck ground, resulting in destruction by post-impact fire (p. 1).

events.text: Aircraft cleared for takeoff from Aurangabad runway; 118 persons on board
Aircraft did not lift off until near the end of 6,000-foot runway with inadequate rotation technique
Left main landing gear and left engine collided with truck carrying cotton bales at approximately 410 feet from runway end
Impact severed left main landing gear and left engine thrust reverser; damaged left elevator and horizontal stabilizer
Aircraft struck high-tension electric power lines approximately 3 km northeast of runway
Aircraft descended and struck ground; fuselage separated and burst into flames due to post-impact fire

safety_changes: Increased airport regulatory enforcement to control vehicular traffic near active runways
Enhanced NOTAMs and ground operations coordination at regional airports
